title: Compile-Time Lookup Tables
hints: The byte is `static_cast<std::uint8_t>(ch)`. If the `static_assert` fails, the compiler stops with the message, which is the point: a wrong table never reaches a running program.
A `consteval` function must run at compile time. Throwing (or calling a function that is not `constexpr`) inside it when the text is bad turns a bad colour into a compile error (lesson 11.04).
requirements: A `constexpr` function that builds a `std::array<std::uint32_t, 256>` CRC-32 table at compile time
A `crc32(std::string_view)` that uses the table; check `crc32("123456789") == 0xCBF43926` with `static_assert`
A `constexpr` table of the first 100 primes, checked with a `static_assert`
A `consteval` function that checks a colour like `"#FF8800"` and refuses bad text at compile time
